name: security-audit
description: Run a defensive security review of a codebase: secrets, dependencies, injection, authz, misconfig, OWASP Top 10. Use when auditing code for vulnerabilities.
checklist: Secrets, deps, injection, authz, config all reviewed

name: security-web
description: Defend web apps against OWASP Top 10: injection, XSS, broken auth/access control, SSRF, misconfig. Use when securing web endpoints.
checklist: Access control enforced server-side per request
Security headers and TLS in place

name: security-secrets
description: Detect and prevent leaked secrets: scanning, .gitignore, env handling, rotation after exposure. Use to find/remove credentials in code or history.
checklist: No secrets in code, config, or git history
Leaked secrets rotated, not just deleted
pitfalls: Deleting a secret from a file but not rotating it

name: security-dependencies
description: Find and fix vulnerable dependencies: audit tools, transitive risk, safe upgrades, lockfiles. Use for dependency/CVE management.

name: security-supply-chain
description: Harden the software supply chain: pinned deps, SBOM, signing, provenance, CI trust boundaries. Use to reduce build/dependency attack surface.

name: security-iam
description: Design least-privilege IAM: roles, policies, scoping, temporary credentials, privilege review. Use for access-control/cloud-IAM design.

name: security-crypto
description: Use cryptography correctly: standard algorithms, key management, hashing vs encryption, no homegrown crypto. Use when handling crypto/hashing.
pitfalls: MD5/SHA1 or unsalted hashes for passwords

name: security-input-validation
description: Validate and sanitize all untrusted input: allowlists, schemas, encoding at the right boundary. Use when handling external input.
checklist: Reject, don't try to sanitize dangerous input silently
pitfalls: Validating but not encoding on output

name: security-xss
description: Prevent cross-site scripting: contextual output encoding, CSP, safe templating, avoiding innerHTML. Use when rendering user content.
pitfalls: No CSP as defense in depth

name: security-sql-injection
description: Prevent SQL/NoSQL injection: parameterized queries, ORMs, no string concatenation, least-privilege DB users. Use when building queries.
checklist: No user input concatenated into queries
pitfalls: Trusting ORMs then dropping to raw concat

name: security-ssrf
description: Prevent server-side request forgery: URL allowlists, blocking internal ranges/metadata endpoints, no user-controlled fetch targets. Use for outbound-request features.

name: security-csrf
description: Prevent cross-site request forgery: anti-CSRF tokens, SameSite cookies, verifying origin. Use for state-changing endpoints with cookie auth.
pitfalls: Relying on cookies without CSRF protection

name: security-headers
description: Set defensive HTTP security headers: CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame options, referrer policy. Use to harden web responses.
pitfalls: Headers set on some routes but not others

name: security-threat-modeling
description: Model threats (STRIDE/attack trees): assets, entry points, trust boundaries, mitigations. Use when designing security-sensitive features.

name: security-sast
description: Run static application security testing (Semgrep/CodeQL): rules, triage, false positives. Use to scan source for vulnerabilities.
pitfalls: Suppressing real findings to pass CI

name: security-dast
description: Run dynamic application security testing against a running app (authorized only): scanning, fuzzing endpoints. Use for authorized black-box testing.
checklist: Explicit authorization to test the target

name: security-pentest-recon
description: Perform authorized reconnaissance and enumeration for pentests/CTFs: scoping, footprinting, service enumeration. Use only with explicit authorization.

name: security-network
description: Harden network security: segmentation, firewalls, least-exposure, TLS everywhere, zero trust. Use when designing/reviewing network exposure.

name: security-container
description: Secure containers: non-root, minimal images, dropped capabilities, read-only FS, image scanning. Use when hardening container workloads.
pitfalls: Running as root with full capabilities
Mounting the Docker socket into containers

name: security-cloud
description: Secure cloud accounts: least-privilege IAM, encryption, public-access prevention, config/CSPM checks. Use when reviewing cloud posture.

name: security-api
description: Secure APIs: authn/authz per endpoint, rate limiting, input validation, object-level authorization, versioned deprecation. Use when securing APIs.

name: security-logging-monitoring
description: Build security logging and detection: audit trails, alerting on suspicious activity, tamper-resistance, no sensitive data in logs. Use for detection/monitoring.
checklist: Alerts on anomalies (failed logins, privilege use)
pitfalls: No audit trail for sensitive actions

name: security-forensics
description: Perform incident forensics: preserve evidence, timeline, indicators of compromise, scope containment. Use during/after a suspected breach.

name: security-compliance
description: Map controls to compliance frameworks (SOC2/ISO27001/GDPR/HIPAA/PCI): evidence, data handling, audits. Use for compliance-driven work.

name: security-mobile
description: Secure mobile apps: secure storage, cert pinning, no secrets in binaries, platform permissions. Use when securing iOS/Android apps.
checklist: Secrets not hardcoded in the app
pitfalls: API keys hardcoded in the binary

name: security-code-review
description: Review code specifically for security defects: taint flow, authz gaps, unsafe deserialization, injection sinks. Use as a security-focused review pass.
checklist: AuthZ checked on every sensitive path
pitfalls: Reviewing style while missing an injection sink
